description: 4 exemplars + 3 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Authored 2026-08-30 under road-to-governed-harness-evolution 2.4, wave 1 (2 inbound confusion edges, no corpus). Exemplars cover the LIVE or just-closed incident — severity, comms cadence, who does what. Near-misses are the two neighbours that named it plus the post-mortem skill that consumes this one's skeleton, which is the sharpest edge because it is the same incident one step later.

queries.q: production is down — what do I do now?
we're ten minutes into an outage; set the severity and the comms cadence
customers are reporting 500s — who does what right now?
wir haben gerade einen Vorfall in Produktion, wie gehen wir vor?
the incident is resolved — run the post-mortem and find the root cause
queries.note: the same incident one step later; facilitation of the blame-free retro consumes this skill's skeleton → blameless-post-mortem

queries.q: which of these alerts deserves to page someone?
queries.note: designing the paging policy in calm time, not running an incident → alerting-doctrine

queries.q: are we ready to go live with this service?
queries.note: a go/no-go before anything has broken → operational-readiness

queries.q: our CI pipeline is red on main
queries.note: a broken build is not a production incident; guards against triggering on any 'X is down/broken' phrasing

queries.q: write the release notes for v3
queries.note: routine release work that mentions shipping and no incident
